title: Integration: Futures of the Sun, Earth and Universe
objective: After this level you can describe the long-term futures of the Sun, Earth, Milky Way and universe.
summary: Polaris won’t stay the pole star. The Sun will brighten, then swell. Andromeda will merge with us, and distant galaxies will slip from view.

cards.headline: Astronomy can forecast billions of years ahead.
cards.body: Your weather app struggles with next Tuesday. Here’s the outlook for the next few billion years: the sky, the Sun, Earth and our galaxy.

events.label: Earth’s axis wobbles through a full circle, so Polaris won’t stay the pole star
A slowly brightening Sun makes Earth too hot for oceans
The Milky Way and Andromeda may merge; a 2025 study put it at about a coin flip
The Sun swells into a red giant, later becoming a white dwarf

cards.headline: The universe’s fate
cards.body: Now zoom all the way out. Level 94 showed dark energy speeding up the expansion. If it keeps doing so, galaxies beyond our local neighborhood will eventually drift out of view. Picture a party where the guests slowly back out the door until only your closest neighbors are left. The Sun’s own story ends quietly: a white dwarf that no longer fuses anything, shining with leftover heat and slowly cooling. No grand finale, just a very long fade.

cards.headline: The future: forecast
learned: Polaris won’t always be the pole star
The Sun will brighten, then become a red giant
Andromeda may merge with the Milky Way
Distant galaxies will drift out of view

questions.prompt: Which of these is expected to happen first?

options.label: The Milky Way and Andromeda may merge
options.rationale: That’s billions of years away, if it happens at all.

options.label: Earth becomes too hot for oceans
The Sun swells into a red giant
The Sun becomes a white dwarf
options.rationale: That comes after the red giant stage.

questions.explanation: A slowly brightening Sun is expected to make Earth too hot for oceans in roughly a billion years, long before the other events.

questions.prompt: Why won’t Polaris always be the North Star?

options.label: Polaris is moving away from Earth
Polaris will burn out very soon
Earth’s axis slowly wobbles in a circle
The Milky Way’s spin will hide it

questions.explanation: Earth’s axis wobbles, tracing a circle about every 26,000 years, so it points at different stars over time.

questions.prompt: From Level 94: if dark energy keeps accelerating the expansion, what happens to distant galaxies?

options.label: They fall back into the Milky Way
They turn into dark matter
options.rationale: Galaxies don’t turn into dark matter.

options.label: They eventually drift out of view

questions.explanation: Accelerating expansion carries distant galaxies away faster and faster, until they move beyond view.
